title: Rectangular bar
spec: Start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, draw a two-dimensional sketch on the first face. Begin the first loop by drawing a line from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.1263, 0.0), then draw a second line from (0.1263, 0.0) to (0.1263, 0.75), followed by a third line from (0.1263, 0.75) to (0.0, 0.75), and finally, a fourth line from (0.0, 0.75) back to the origin. After completing the sketch, apply a scale factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero degrees and translating it with a vector set to zero. Finally, extrude the two-dimensional sketch 0.0237 units along the normal direction to create a three-dimensional solid body. The final dimensions of the rectangular bar will be a length of 0.126315789473684 units, a width of 0.7499999999999994 units, and a height of 0.02368421052631577 units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1263, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.1263, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.75) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular bar
r = r.extrude(0.0237)

# The final model is represented as 'r'

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0237) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0237) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.1263)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90.0, 0.0, -90.0) and the translation vector is (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the model 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
